### Target customer
Office-goers in Indiranagar who skip lunch at their desk

### Offer in 40-80 words
Busy in Indiranagar and ending up with a samosa at 3 pm? Our home-style lunch box reaches your desk by 12:45, cooked that morning with less oil than a canteen meal. Weekday plans start with a small trial of five lunches. Tap the link to see this week’s menu and pick your first day.

### Claim to verify before publishing
Delivery by 12:45 on every weekday across Indiranagar offices

### Your reasoning
I picked office-goers because their problem is clear: they have no time and settle for snacks. The delivery time is the claim I would check first, because if the kitchen cannot keep it, the offer breaks its own promise and people lose trust.

### Campaign goal
Menu enquiries on WhatsApp

### Tone to ask for
Warm and homely

### Reusable AI prompt
Write three ad hooks for a home-meal service in Bengaluru. Audience: office-goers in Indiranagar who skip proper lunch. Goal: menu enquiries on WhatsApp. Evidence you may use: weekday menu, delivery area is Indiranagar only, delivery by 12:45. Do not invent reviews, ratings, health claims or customer names. Use one call to action only. Tone: warm and homely. Output: three hooks, each in under 20 words, with one line on why it could work.

### Quality checklist for the AI output
1. Every fact matches the evidence I gave.
2. No invented review, number or health claim.
3. Exactly one action for the reader.
4. Hook is under 20 words and sounds warm.
5. The three hooks differ in angle, not just wording.

### Your reasoning
I gave the AI only real facts so it has nothing to make up, and I banned reviews and health claims because those need proof. The checklist lets me judge the hooks calmly instead of liking whichever sounds smoothest.

### Link
https://docs.google.com/document/d/example-ai-prompt

### First reply to the prospect
Hi Anita, thanks for asking about the menu. This week we have a vegetarian and a mixed option, both with delivery to your office park in Indiranagar. Which one would you like to see first?

### One follow-up message
Hi Anita, just checking if the vegetarian menu works for you. If you tell me your office floor and timing, I can confirm if we deliver there. No rush at all.

### Opt-out line
Reply STOP any time and we will not message you again.

### Conversion measure
Share of prospects who ask for a trial

### Your reasoning
I answered the practical question first so the message helps before it asks. A trial request is a better measure than replies alone, because someone can reply politely and still not want the lunch. The opt-out line keeps it respectful.

### Interview group
People who tried a tiffin service and stopped

### Fair rewrite of the leading question
How do you usually decide what to eat for lunch on a workday?

### Five questions
1. Tell me about your last weekday lunch from start to finish.
2. How did you decide where that lunch came from?
3. What happened the last time you tried a tiffin service?
4. What made you stop, or switch to something else?
5. What do you do on days when lunch goes wrong?

### Your reasoning
I picked people who stopped a tiffin service because they can explain real reasons, not guesses. My rewrite is fairer than the yes/no version because it does not push home food as the right answer, so the person tells me how they really decide.

### Biggest risk
A job guarantee the team cannot control

### Problems found
1. “Guaranteed job in 30 days” cannot be promised because employers decide.
2. “Only 3 seats left” looks like fake urgency if seats are not limited.
3. Adding PDF downloaders to a promotions list without asking them.

### Ad rewrite
Build a stronger resume in four weeks with feedback on every draft. The fee is ₹1,499 and we cannot promise a job.

### Consent step
On the PDF download page I would add an unticked box: “Send me course offers on WhatsApp.” The first message says what I will send and each message ends with “Reply STOP to leave.”

The job guarantee is the biggest risk because someone might pay money expecting a result nobody controls. My rewrite only says what the course gives, feedback and a resume, so I can prove it. Asking before adding people respects their choice.

### User story
As a parent, I want to request a trial class in a free evening slot so that my child can try the tutor before I pay for a full month.

### Fields to collect
Parent name (to greet them), phone number (so the tutor can confirm on WhatsApp), child's class (to prepare the right level), preferred slot (the main request). No email or address because the tutor does not need them.

### Three acceptance checks
1. Given a free slot, when the parent submits name, phone and slot, then the server saves it and only then shows Booking saved.
2. Given a slot already taken, when submitted, then the server refuses it and shows the free slots.
3. Given an empty name or a 6-digit phone, then nothing is saved and the form says which field to fix.

### One failure state
Sorry, that slot was just taken. Please choose another time from the list below.

### Most private detail
Parent's phone number

### Your reasoning
The phone number is the most private because anyone who sees it can call or message the family, so only the tutor should see it. I kept the fields short because every extra field is more data to protect and more checks to write. The saved message comes after storage so a parent is never told a lie.

### Tables and columns
CREATE TABLE batches (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  starts_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  capacity INT NOT NULL CHECK (capacity > 0)
);
CREATE TABLE bookings (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  batch_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES batches(id),
  seat_no INT NOT NULL,
  parent_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  parent_phone TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (batch_id, seat_no)
);

### What must never repeat
One row per seat number in one batch

### Private columns and who sees them
parent_phone and parent_name in bookings. Only the tutor can read them, and a parent can see only their own row. Other parents should see only how many seats are left.

### Your reasoning
I made batch_id and seat_no unique together because the problem is two people getting the same seat, and the database checks this at save time even when two clicks arrive together. A phone number is private because anyone holding it can contact a family, so the tutor alone reads it.

### Launch checklist
launch_checklist:
  - [ ] security: does a request for another family's booking return 404 or 403?
  - [ ] tests: do the seat boundary and negative tests all pass in CI?
  - [ ] privacy: is parent_phone hidden from every page except the tutor's?
  - [ ] errors: does a failed save show "please try again" and not "confirmed"?
  - [ ] monitoring: does the tutor get a WhatsApp alert after 3 failed saves?

### Risk to fix first
Any family can open another family's booking

### Who is alerted, and how
The tutor gets a WhatsApp message from the server if three saves fail within ten minutes.

### Why that risk comes first
Changing the booking number is easy to try and likely once fifty families are using the app, and the harm is real: phone numbers of other parents are exposed. The typo and slow loading hurt less. After the fix I will retest with a second parent login to confirm the 404.

### Your reasoning
I ranked the gaps by harm and likelihood: the booking-number gap is both easy to try and harmful because it leaks private phone numbers, so it goes before alerts, speed or spelling. Each check is a yes or no question so I can answer it honestly instead of feeling vaguely worried.

### Logline
A Bengaluru delivery rider, racing a deadline, finds a child’s handmade birthday card in a parcel bag and must decide whether to lose time returning it.

### Feeling at the end
Warmth: a small kindness lands

### Beat 1: Setup
The rider stops at an apartment gate, checks the clock, and a handmade card slips out of the bag.

### Beat 2: Choice
He sees the name on the card, looks at his phone timer, and chooses to walk it to the watchman.

### Beat 3: Payoff
The lonely watchman reads the card, then smiles, and the rider rides off with a lighter face.

### Your reasoning
The choice shows the rider cares more about a stranger’s feeling than his own time, which tells us his character without any speech. I picked warmth because he pays a small cost and gets only a smile back.

### Six-shot list
1 | wide | rider arrives at the apartment gate | 5s | hurry
2 | close-up | card slips out of the bag | 4s | surprise
3 | reaction | rider checks the time on his phone | 5s | pressure
4 | detail | name on the card is read | 5s | curiosity
5 | medium | rider hands the card to the watchman | 6s | kindness
6 | close-up | the watchman’s worry becomes a smile | 5s | warmth

### Size of the final shot
Close-up on the watchman’s face

### Cut into the choice moment
Cutaway to the card, then back to the rider

### One continuity rule
The rider keeps the same red jacket, bag on the left shoulder, and the gate stays on the right of frame.

### One sound cue
A phone timer ticks in shots 3 and 4, then stops the moment the card is handed over.

### Your reasoning
The order goes from arrival to discovery, to checking the time, to the choice, to the handover and the smile, so each shot adds new information. I chose the watchman’s close-up last because the smile is the payoff of the whole story.

### Live-action and AI-assisted elements
Live: rider, watchman, card close-ups, ambient sound, because performance and small details are easy to capture well.
AI-assisted: storyboard ideas and a colour look test, because they help planning without touching the performers.

### Budget split in rupees
Phone gimbal hire: ₹800
Two performer meals and chai: ₹600
Handmade card props: ₹300
Transport: ₹900
Room tone recorder rental: ₹700
Contingency: ₹500
Total: ₹3,800

### Continuity and final quality checks
Same jacket, bag and time of day in each shot. Eyelines match across the cut. Colour looks the same between live and test frames. Voices and ambience are clean and level. Credits and licences checked before sharing.

### Consent or asset-rights check
Written note plus a licence check for every generated asset

### One thing I will not generate
The watchman’s smile, because it must be a real performance.

### Your reasoning
Reshooting the smile live is free and keeps a real performance, which matters more to the story than a polished generated face. I use AI only for planning, so the continuity of light and clothes stays under my control.
